title: RN start of care, assisted living, questions out of order

turns.text: Hi Gloria, I'm Priya from the agency. I'll be quick, I know you have bingo at two.
You know me already. Go ahead, honey.
Any pain lately? Over the past 5 days, how much has pain made it hard to sleep at night?
My shoulder aches during the day, but it never keeps me up. I sleep like a baby.
How often has that shoulder made you cut back on what you do during the day?
Now and then. I skipped chair yoga twice this week.
Do you ever get short of breath?
No, my lungs are fine. I walk the whole hallway twice a day.
Good. Date of birth for my records?
April 30th, fifty-seven.
You're here at Magnolia Court, so the staff is around 24 hours, right?
Day and night. They check on me at breakfast and at bedtime, and there's a call button by the bed.
What insurance are you using for home health now?
The Medicare Advantage plan, the one through the retirement association.
Are you of Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin?
No.
And your race?
I'd rather not say, if that's alright.
Of course. You prefer English for your care, and no interpreter?
English, and no interpreter, thank you.
Before this infection, did you need any help with bathing, dressing, the bathroom, or eating?
None. I do it all myself.
Walking around your apartment, and the stairs down to the dining room?
I walk everywhere on my own, and I take the stairs to the dining room, no help. The elevator's too slow.
And keeping track of your pills and errands?
I fill my own pill box. And I make my own lists for the shuttle.
Any devices before, a walker, a wheelchair, a brace?
Just my leg brace. I've worn it since the polio when I was a girl.
Let me do the memory part. I am going to say three words for you to remember. Please repeat the words after I have said all three. The words are sock, blue, and bed. Now tell me the three words.
Sock, blue, bed.
Please tell me what year it is right now.
Twenty twenty-six.
What month are we in right now?
October. Just started.
What day of the week is today?
Thursday. Bingo day.
How often do you feel lonely or isolated from those around you?
Rarely. There's always somebody knocking on my door here.
Any falls, weight loss, ER visits, or trips to the hospital this year?
None of that. The infection was handled by my regular doctor, I never went in.
And you're feeling okay, not worn out?
I feel fine. A little tired from the antibiotics, but those are done now.
What medicines are you on now?
Levothyroxine, vitamin D, and amlodipine. The antibiotic finished on Monday.
Great. I'll skip the weight today, the scale's in my car. We'll do it Monday.

notes: Not discussed, must abstain: M1060A-B (scale in the car). Traps: pain exists but does not affect sleep (J0510 is 1, not 0); antibiotic already finished, so N0415 is Z; leg brace is an orthotic (E); questions come out of form order.
